title: Measurement of Left Ventricular Performance in Langendorff Perfused Mouse Hearts
author: E. Dale Abel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7tfhnjn
materials: Left ventricle systolic pressure (LVSP): Units mmHg. (
Heart Rate (HR): Units beats per minute (

steps.title: Isolate and Cannulate Heart
steps.instruction: Isolate the heart and cannulate the aorta using a 20g steel cannula.

steps.title: Initiate Constant Pressure Perfusion
steps.instruction: Perfuse the heart at a constant pressure of 60 mmHg using warm (37°C) Krebs buffer gassed with 95% O2 and 5% CO2.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Krebs buffer containing (in mM): 118 NaCl, 4.7 KCl, 25 NaHCO3, 1.2 MgSO4, 1.2 KH2PO4, and 2 CaCl2.
Perfuse with 11mM glucose as the sole substrate, or in combination with 1 or 1.2 mM palmitate.

steps.title: Prepare Venous Drainage and Pressure Monitoring
steps.instruction: Set up the heart for drainage and pressure measurement.

substeps.instruction: Transect the pulmonary artery to facilitate coronary venous drainage.
Insert a polyethylene apical drain into the left ventricle through a left atrial incision to allow thebesian venous drainage.
Place a water-filled balloon through the left atrial appendage and connect it to a Millar transducer to monitor left ventricular pressure.
Adjust the balloon volume to achieve a left ventricular diastolic pressure of 7 mmHg.

steps.title: Set Pacing Rate
steps.instruction: Adjust heart rates to 360 beats/min by pacing at 6 Hz at the level of the atria.

steps.title: Acquire Baseline Data
steps.instruction: Allow the heart to stabilize for 30 min, then acquire data under baseline conditions (buffer calcium concentration = 2 mM).

steps.title: Measure High-Calcium Contractile Parameters
steps.instruction: Switch the perfusion to a second buffer containing 4 mM CaCl2 and measure contractile parameters after another 20 min of stabilization.

steps.title: Sample Coronary Effluent and Measure Oxygen
steps.instruction: Sample coronary effluent from the pulmonary artery using a capillary tube and measure oxygen content using an Oxygen foxy probe (OceanOptics).

substeps.instruction: Calculate oxygen content using O2 solubility (23.9 μl/ml) and O2 density (0.03933 μmol/μl) in a solution at 37°C.

steps.title: Calculate Performance Parameters
steps.instruction: Determine the following cardiac parameters from the acquired data:

substeps.instruction: Left ventricle systolic pressure (LVSP) in mmHg.
Left ventricle developed pressure (LVDP or LVDevP) = LVSP – LV Diastolic pressure (mmHg).
Heart Rate (HR) in beats per minute.
Rate Pressure Product (RPP) = LVDP x HR (mmHg/sec).
dP/dtmin and dP/dtmax (maximal rates of LV pressure decay and development) in mmHg/msec.
Coronary Flow (ml/min) by measuring coronary effluent.
Cardiac efficiency as the ratio of RPP/MVO2 expressed as a percentage.
